title: VFD3-P1: joint resource bounds and zero fractional tolerance

claims.statement: For every integer N >= 2 and every fixed secret s in Z/NZ, let n=ceil(log2 N). The single VFD3 algorithm and exact parameter choice in proof.md Sections 1-10, with its specified n<=16 exhaustive branch, recover the entire secret with unconditional probability at least 1019/1024. All three bounds hold jointly on every execution branch, with absolute constants independent of N, s and outcomes. For n>=2, total charged sequential work T is O(n^5 2^((4899/2000) sqrt(n))); the explicitly bounded n=1 cases are handled separately. This full envelope includes all costs and storage assigned to that resource in rules.md. Its growth index is exactly 1/2. The structured bound is this same envelope, with the known coefficient 4899/2000 inside the exponent and an unspecified absolute outer big-O constant.

For every integer N >= 2 and every fixed secret s in Z/NZ, let n=ceil(log2 N). The single VFD3 algorithm and exact parameter choice in proof.md Sections 1-10, with its specified n<=16 exhaustive branch, recover the entire secret with unconditional probability at least 1019/1024. All three bounds hold jointly on every execution branch, with absolute constants independent of N, s and outcomes. For n>=2, peak allocated classical space S_C in bits is O(n^(3/2) 2^((4899/2000) sqrt(n))); the explicitly bounded n=1 cases are handled separately. This full envelope includes all costs and storage assigned to that resource in rules.md. Its growth index is exactly 1/2. The structured bound is this same envelope, with the known coefficient 4899/2000 inside the exponent and an unspecified absolute outer big-O constant.

For every integer N >= 2 and every fixed secret s in Z/NZ, let n=ceil(log2 N). The single VFD3 algorithm and exact parameter choice in proof.md Sections 1-10, with its specified n<=16 exhaustive branch, recover the entire secret with unconditional probability at least 1019/1024. All three bounds hold jointly on every execution branch, with absolute constants independent of N, s and outcomes. For n>=2, peak allocated accessible quantum space S_Q in qubits is O(n^(1/2) 2^((4899/2000) sqrt(n))); the explicitly bounded n=1 cases are handled separately. This full envelope includes all costs and storage assigned to that resource in rules.md. Its growth index is exactly 1/2. The structured bound is this same envelope, with the known coefficient 4899/2000 inside the exponent and an unspecified absolute outer big-O constant.

For every integer N >= 2 and fixed secret s in Z/NZ, let n=ceil(log2 N). For the same VFD3 algorithm and exact configuration in proof.md, on every execution branch including aborts, the total number K of fresh DCP source copies acquired is at most N(n+10) for n<=16 and at most 4(J+1)L_0+(n+10)(2^ell+2) for n>=17, with J, L_0 and ell defined in proof.md Section 1. Consequently K=O(n^(3/2) 2^((4899/2000) sqrt(n))) uniformly over N, s and outcomes, with an absolute outer constant; the n=1 cases are explicitly covered by the finite branch. The envelope has exact growth index 1/2. The count includes all batch acquisitions and fresh verification copies, including rejected tests, failed attempts and discarded copies. This bound holds jointly with the original time and memory guarantees and unconditional success at least 1019/1024 under the specified ideal independent source. The structured object describes this same sample-count envelope.

For every integer N>=2, every fixed secret s in Z/NZ and n=ceil(log2 N), the same VFD3 algorithm and exact configuration in proof.md has guaranteed fractional malformed-sample tolerance epsilon(n)=0. If Q copies are acquired, at most floor(epsilon(n) Q)=0 acquisitions may violate the ideal-source promise, and all acquired copies must be independent copies of rho_s for that fixed s, as specified in metrics-addendum.md Section 3. Under this promise, unconditional full-secret success is at least 1019/1024, jointly with all four declared worst-case resource bounds. No positive corruption tolerance or guarantee for malformed copies is asserted. Zero is a guaranteed fraction, not a proof that greater tolerance is impossible, not a per-copy corruption probability, and not the internal failure probability. This fractional-expression claim has no numeric score.

structured.error_model: Malformed fraction among acquired copies. The proved guarantee requires every copy to be an independent ideal coset state; no behavior is promised for malformed copies.
